# Investigation Summary

## Symptoms

### Automated flood from 198.51.100.10 passed through WAF (168,126 requests allowed)
**Description:** A single US source IP 198.51.100.10, using the load-testing user-agent "Artillery (https://artillery.io)", sent 168,126 requests that were ALL ALLOWED during 2026-10-10 17:00:00–18:15:00 UTC. Traffic was concentrated on checkout/cart endpoints (POST /checkout/payment, /cart, /checkout, /checkout/delivery). The WAF rate-based rule counted the flood but blocked nothing.
**Time:** 2026-10-10T17:00:00Z - 2026-10-10T18:15:00Z

## Findings

### Cause: Rate-based rule in COUNT mode did not block the abuse
**Description:** Web ACL rule AWS-RateBasedRule-IP-300-CreatedByCloudFront (limit 300/5min/IP) is configured with Action=COUNT, not Block. It COUNTED 168,584 requests in the window but blocked zero — so the single-IP flood (168k requests, far over the 300/5min threshold) passed through to the origin. This is why the high-volume abuse was detected but not blocked.
**Cascades to:** symptom-rate-abuse

### Hypothesis: Card-testing / checkout-abuse campaign allowed through (198.51.100.10, UA Artillery)
**Description:** A single IP 198.51.100.10 (US, User-Agent `Artillery`) ran a tight automated loop through the full checkout funnel — GET /cart (23,922), POST /cart (14,678), POST /checkout/payment (9,262), POST /checkout/delivery (9,260), POST /checkout (9,257). Combined with secondary IP 198.51.100.30 (1,350 payment POSTs, browser-spoofing UA), 10,612 POST /checkout/payment requests from just 2 IPs were 100% ALLOWED. Behavioral signature of automated payment/card-testing abuse. Remains a HYPOTHESIS for fraud intent: WAF logs show empty responsecodesent for ALLOWed requests, so per-attempt payment success/decline cannot be confirmed from WAF logs alone — correlate with CloudFront/origin access logs.
**Cascades to:** symptom-rate-abuse

#### Gaps
- **Many sensitive-path scans returned ALLOW:** Path-scanning probes for secrets (.env, .git/HEAD, .aws/credentials, wp-config.php.bak, web.config, phpinfo.php) from 198.51.100.20 were only partially blocked. A large set of probe URIs were allowed through because they matched no managed rule, leaving a coverage gap for sensitive-path/secret-file reconnaissance.

### Hypothesis: Sensitive-path scanning (198.51.100.20) — partly blocked, many probes allowed
**Description:** IP 198.51.100.20 (US, spoofed Chrome UA) enumerated sensitive files across 5 directory prefixes (/, /dev/, /test/, /old/, /backup/): .aws/credentials, .env/.env.bak, wp-config.php.bak, web.config. WAF BLOCKED 25 of these (15 RestrictedExtensions_URIPATH + 5 GenericLFI_URIPATH on CommonRuleSet, 5 ExploitablePaths_URIPATH on KnownBadInputs), but a large set of probe paths (e.g. /.env, /.git/HEAD, /phpinfo.php, /backup/*.sql) still returned ALLOW because no rule matched them.
**Cascades to:** symptom-rate-abuse

#### Gaps
- **Many sensitive-path scans returned ALLOW:** Path-scanning probes for secrets (.env, .git/HEAD, .aws/credentials, wp-config.php.bak, web.config, phpinfo.php) from 198.51.100.20 were only partially blocked. # Mitigation Summary

## Action
Close the WAF detect-not-block gap: switch the rate-based rule AWS-RateBasedRule-IP-300-CreatedByCloudFront (priority 1) from Count to Block on Web ACL CreatedByCloudFront-a1b2c3d4, and add a dedicated IP-set Block rule for the two confirmed checkout-abuse source IPs (198.51.100.10, 198.51.100.30).

## Reasoning
During 2026-10-10 17:00–18:15 UTC the priority-1 rate-based rule was Action=Count: it detected 168,584 matches but blocked nothing, letting an automated card-testing / checkout-abuse campaign through to origin (168,126 req from 198.51.100.10 / UA Artillery; 1,350 POST /checkout/payment from 198.51.100.30; 100% of payment POSTs ALLOWED). Capacity used is 1177/5000, leaving room for a new rule. Switching to Block enforces across the whole checkout funnel; the explicit IP-set Block gives deterministic blocking independent of rate thresholds (preferred over a UA-string block since UAs are trivially spoofed). Limit stays at 300/5min to avoid collateral impact. Both are bounded, reversible WAF config edits.

## Execution Plan

### Step 1: Prepare

#### 1.1 Capture the complete current Web ACL config as the authoritative…
**Type:** command
```
aws wafv2 get-web-acl --name CreatedByCloudFront-a1b2c3d4 --scope CLOUDFRONT --id f0598f76-f04d-456a-beff-5521b48914d4 --region us-east-1 > webacl-backup-CreatedByCloudFront-a1b2c3d4.json
```
**Purpose:** Capture the complete current Web ACL config as the authoritative rollback baseline before any change.
**Advisory:** Confirm the saved file corresponds to this exact Web ACL (id f0598f76-f04d-456a-beff-5521b48914d4) before relying on it for rollback.

#### 1.2 Create a dedicated IP set with the two confirmed abuser IPs; record the…
**Type:** command
```
aws wafv2 create-ip-set --name checkout-abuse-blocklist-CreatedByCloudFront --scope CLOUDFRONT --ip-address-version IPV4 --addresses 198.51.100.10/32 198.51.100.30/32 --description "Confirmed card-testing/checkout-abuse source IPs (incident 2026-10-10)" --region us-east-1
```
**Purpose:** Create a dedicated IP set with the two confirmed abuser IPs; record the returned Id/ARN for the apply step.
**Advisory:** Use a new dedicated IP set, not the unrelated existing example-bot-dev-blocked-ips set (different app, not referenced by this Web ACL).

### Step 2: Pre Validate

#### 2.1 Re-fetch a fresh LockToken immediately before the update and confirm…
**Type:** command
```
aws wafv2 get-web-acl --name CreatedByCloudFront-a1b2c3d4 --scope CLOUDFRONT --id f0598f76-f04d-456a-beff-5521b48914d4 --region us-east-1 --query 'LockToken'
```
**Purpose:** Re-fetch a fresh LockToken immediately before the update and confirm the priority-1 rule is still Action=Count; re-capture the backup if the live Rules array differs.
**Advisory:** The LockToken seen during investigation (36528525-b4de-4ef9-acfc-17bebab7891f) is likely stale and must not be reused.

### Step 3: Apply

#### 3.1 Enforce volumetric blocking across the checkout funnel and…
**Type:** text
Submit a single update-web-acl using the FULL Rules array from the prepare backup with exactly two changes: (1) priority-1 rule AWS-RateBasedRule-IP-300-CreatedByCloudFront Action {Count:{}} -> {Block:{}} (keep Limit=300, EvaluationWindowSec=300, AggregateKeyType=IP); (2) append a Priority 6 rule 'Block-CheckoutAbuse-IPSet' with Action {Block:{}} and an IPSetReferenceStatement to the new IP set ARN, VisibilityConfig MetricName=Block-CheckoutAbuse-IPSet. Keep DefaultAction=Allow and all managed rule groups (AntiDDoS p0, IpReputation p2, Common p3, KnownBadInputs p4, SQLi p5) unchanged. Pass the fresh LockToken from pre_validate.
**Purpose:** Enforce volumetric blocking across the checkout funnel and deterministically block the two confirmed abuser IPs — directly closing the detect-not-block root cause.
**Risks:** Blocking at 300 req/5min per IP could affect a legitimate client exceeding that from a single IP (large NAT/corporate egress); monitor BlockedRequests and raise the limit or add an exception if false positives appear., The explicit IP block denies all traffic from 198.51.100.10 and 198.51.100.30; remove an address if it is later reassigned to a legitimate user.
**Advisory:** update-web-acl requires the full Rules array — omitting any rule silently removes it, so build from the prepare backup. The added rule is well within remaining capacity (1177/5000).

### Step 4: Post Validate

#### 4.1 Confirm priority-1 is now Action=Block, a priority-6…
**Type:** command
```
aws wafv2 get-web-acl --name CreatedByCloudFront-a1b2c3d4 --scope CLOUDFRONT --id f0598f76-f04d-456a-beff-5521b48914d4 --region us-east-1
```
**Purpose:** Confirm priority-1 is now Action=Block, a priority-6 IPSetReferenceStatement Block rule is present, and all other rules + DefaultAction=Allow are unchanged.

#### 4.2 Confirm the rate-based rule now produces BlockedRequests when abuse…
**Type:** command
```
aws cloudwatch get-metric-statistics --namespace AWS/WAFV2 --metric-name BlockedRequests --dimensions Name=WebACL,Value=CreatedByCloudFront-a1b2c3d4 Name=Region,Value=CloudFront Name=Rule,Value=AWS-RateBasedRule-IP-300-CreatedByCloudFront --start-time 2026-10-10T18:30:00Z --end-time 2026-10-10T19:30:00Z --period 300 --statistics Sum --region us-east-1
```
**Purpose:** Confirm the rate-based rule now produces BlockedRequests when abuse traffic is present, verifying enforcement rather than count-only.
**Advisory:** Adjust the time window to a period containing live traffic; the window shown is an example just after the incident.

### Step 5: Rollback

#### 5.1 Restore the exact pre-change rule set so the change is fully reversible
**Type:** text
Re-fetch the current LockToken, then update-web-acl restoring the exact Rules array from webacl-backup-CreatedByCloudFront-a1b2c3d4.json (priority-1 Action back to {Count:{}}, remove the priority-6 rule), keeping DefaultAction=Allow. Lighter-touch alternative that keeps enforcement: remove individual addresses from the IP set (update-ip-set) or raise the rate Limit above 300.
**Purpose:** Restore the exact pre-change rule set so the change is fully reversible.
**Risks:** Reverting the rate rule to Count re-opens the detect-not-block gap; prefer the lighter-touch rollback for a specific false positive.
**Advisory:** The IP set cannot be deleted while referenced by the Web ACL; remove the priority-6 rule first if you also intend to delete the IP set.
